sample_unit: chatbot responses (7 questions x 3 vignettes x 3 repetitions)

links.outcome: Differences in chatbot response quality across Black, White, and race-agnostic vignettes
links.effect: No significant racial differences in comprehensiveness (mean 67%), inaccuracies (32%), readability, actionability (92%), or DISCERN (14/18); question-1 comprehensiveness lower for Black vs race-agnostic vignette (60% vs 93%, P<.01).
links.quote: We identified no statistically significant racial disparities across the five evaluation domains in ProGene.

links.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot patient education responses
links.effect: Mean readability was 10th grade (SMOG) and 13th grade (Flesch-Kincaid); none varied by race.
links.quote: The mean readability were 10th (SMOG) and 13th (Flesch-Kincaid) grades, actionability 92%, and DISCERN score 14/18 (good quality); none varied by race.

screen.reason: Evaluates a generative AI chatbot (ProGene) for racial bias across simulated patient vignettes, but does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
